photo.fileTitle: File:Austronesian maritime trade network in the Indian Ocean.png
photo.caption: Austronesian proto-historic and historic (Maritime Silk Road) maritime trade network in Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean
photo.description: Proto-historic and historic maritime trade network of the Austronesian peoples in the Indian Ocean per "Austronesian Shipping in the Indian Ocean: From Outrigger Boats to Trading Ships" in (2016) Early Exchange between Africa and the Wider Indian Ocean World, Palgrave Macmillan, pp. 51−76 ISBN: 9783319338224.

photo.caption: Jade lingling-o pendants from the Austronesian Sa Huỳnh culture of southern Vietnam (c. 2,500-2,200 BP). These were traded in ancient maritime trade routes from 2000 BCE to 1000 BCE, largely between the Philippines, southern Vietnam, Borneo, and Taiwan, across the South China Sea
photo.description: Earings - Gem, Sa Huynh culture Collections of the Museum of Vietnamese History Circa 2,500~2,200 years ago From Phu Hoa, Đồng Nai Province

photo.caption: Ruins of the Mỹ Sơn Hindu temple complex (c. 4th century CE) of the Austronesian Champa polities of central and southern Vietnam, along the main route of the Maritime Silk Road
photo.description: Building B5 of Group B, Mỹ Sơn sanctuary, Vietnam.

photo.caption: One of the Borobudur ships from the 8th century, they were depictions of large Javanese outrigger vessels. Shown with the characteristic tanja sail of Southeast Asian Austronesians
photo.description: Relief panel of a ship at Borobudur

photo.caption: Asia in the 14th century showing the maximum extent of Majapahit and its relative position to other participants of the Maritime Silk Road
photo.description: Approximate outlines of nations in Asia in 1335.

rights.fileTitle: File:16th century Portuguese Spanish trade routes.png

photo.fileTitle: File:16th century Portuguese Spanish trade routes.png
photo.caption: Global Trade Routes of the Spanish and Portuguese Empire
photo.description: Map showing main Portuguese (blue) and Spanish (white) oceanic trade routes in the 16th century, as a result of the exploration during the Age of Discovery. Showing the Spanish colonial Manila-Acapulco Galleons route (1565-1815) between the Viceroyalty of New Spain (México) and the Spanish East Indies (Philippines), using the ports of Acapulco and Cavite. PIA03395: World in Mercator Projection, Shaded Relief and Colored Height Portuguese Spanish Portuguese Spanish

photo.fileTitle: File:Planks of a Butuan balangay in the Butuan National Museum.jpg
photo.caption: Planks from one of the Butuan ship burials (c. 689 to 988 CE) from the Philippines, showing protruding lugs and holes where dowels were inserted in the distinctively Austronesian lashed-lug shipbuilding tradition
photo.description: Planks of the Butuan balangay in the Balangay Shrine Museum

photo.fileTitle: File:Samudra Raksa dari depan, dengan layar terkembang seperti sayap angsa.jpg
photo.caption: The Samudra Raksa, a modern replica of the 8th century Javanese double outrigger trade ships found in the Borobudur temple
photo.description: The Borobudur ship (Samudra Raksa) seen from the front, expanding its sails like a swan (goose-winged/running before the wind, receiving wind from aft).
